issues.legal_issue: A Family Court has jurisdiction over a property dispute between former spouses when the claimed property is connected to their relationship as spouses.
material_facts: The parties had been married and were divorced before the property suit was filed.
One former spouse claimed that property had been purchased using money and jewellery provided in connection with the marriage and sought recognition of her interest in it.
The other former spouse disputed the claim and challenged the agreement concerning the property.
The Family Court decided the property dispute, and the High Court upheld its jurisdiction and decision.
issues.conclusion: The Family Court had jurisdiction to decide the property dispute even though the marriage had ended before the suit was brought.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 and Explanation (c) of the Family Courts Act, 1984, read in light of the Act’s object of resolving family disputes, extend to property claimed by one spouse against the other whether the claim is made during or after the marriage. The phrase “parties to a marriage” does not mean only parties to a subsisting marriage. The Court agreed with the Kerala High Court’s decision in 1997 (1) KLT 734. It distinguished Amjum Hasan Siddiqui v. Smt. Salma B. (AIR 1992 Allahabad 322), which concerned an application under the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986, and Smt. P. Jayalakshmi v. V. Revichandran (AIR 1992 AP 190), which concerned a separate proceeding under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

predicates.family_court_property_proceeding: A proceeding was brought before a Family Court to resolve a dispute about property.
predicates.dispute_between_spouses_or_former_spouse: The property dispute was between people who were or had been married to each other.
predicates.property_claimed_in_spousal_capacity: A party claimed the property through an asserted connection to the parties’ relationship as spouses.

issues.definition: When a Family Court property proceeding concerns a dispute between spouses or former spouses over property claimed in spousal capacity, the Family Court has jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A proceeding to determine rights in property between former spouses is not barred merely because a separate proceeding for relief on divorce has resulted in an award.
material_facts: The respondent had obtained an award in an application seeking relief following divorce.
The present proceeding concerned the parties’ rights in property.
The Court found that the two proceedings were separate and distinct.
issues.conclusion: The prior award in the divorce-related proceeding did not make the property proceeding unmaintainable.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the divorce-related application and the property proceeding were separate and distinct. It rejected the contention that the award in the former proceeding barred the latter.

predicates.property_rights_proceeding: A party brought a proceeding to determine rights in property against a former spouse.
predicates.prior_divorce_relief_proceeding: A party had pursued a separate proceeding for relief arising from the divorce.
predicates.proceedings_concern_distinct_rights: The two proceedings concerned distinct rights or claims.

issues.definition: When a property-rights proceeding and a prior divorce-relief proceeding concern distinct rights, the prior proceeding does not bar the property proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A final determination between the same parties on the Family Court’s jurisdiction to hear their property dispute binds those parties in a later challenge.
material_facts: A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court had previously decided, in a dispute between the same parties, that a dispute over property between parties to a marriage was not limited to parties whose marriage was still subsisting.
The appellant later challenged the Family Court’s jurisdiction in the property dispute.
issues.conclusion: The prior final determination between the parties operated as res judicata on the jurisdiction issue.
issues.legal_principle: The Court agreed with the prior Division Bench decision and held that, because it was between the same parties and had attained finality, it operated as res judicata.

predicates.later_jurisdiction_challenge: A party later challenged the tribunal’s authority to hear the dispute.
predicates.prior_final_interparty_determination_on_: A prior final decision between the same parties had determined the same jurisdiction issue.

issues.definition: When a party later raises a jurisdiction issue already finally determined between the same parties, that prior determination binds them.
